thread.title: Report: People can’t stop walking into glass at Apple’s new headquarters

author: Luke Stangel
title: Report: People can’t stop walking into glass at Apple’s new headquarters

organizations.name: u.s. occupational safety and health administration

text: – Contributing writer Feb 16, 2018, 3:14pm EST Apple Inc.'s sparkling new headquarters in Cupertino, California might be a little too futuristic for the company’s employees, who apparently keep running into glass doors and walls there, MarketWatch reports . In early January, two men were separately treated for minor cuts after walking into glass at Apple’s headquarters, according to public records obtained by MarketWatch . It’s unclear how many people walk into the glass at Apple Park every day, as the majority of those accidents aren’t serious enough to be reported. U.S. Occupational Safety and Health Administration regulations require employers to clearly mark glass doors, walls and barriers to prevent injuries. At other large Silicon Valley companies, that means frosted glass accents, stylized graphics, and other visual cues. OSHA regulators have reportedly not cited Apple yet for any glass-related safety violations at Apple Park. Apple (Nasdaq: AAPL) began moving in employees into the doughnut-shaped Apple Park en masse earlier this year, despite the campus still being under construction. Apple is not allowing outside visitors onto the campus, restricting access to badged employees. The closest outsiders can get is the Apple Park Visitor Center across the street. The company apparently discourages employees from posting photos of the inside of the campus on social media, given the dearth of Apple Park photos on Instagram. Asked about that decision earlier this week at Apple’s annual investor meeting, CEO Tim Cook said it was because there was a high risk a visitor might see something confidential, possibly because there’s so much clear glass everywhere. Many employees also apparently weren't thrilled, at least initially, with the open floor office layout at the campus.
